questions.question: Which of the following is the correct way to open a file named 'notes.txt' just to read its content?
questions.explanation: To read a file, you use the `open()` function with the `'r'` (read) mode. Note that `'r'` is also the default if you don't specify a mode.

questions.question: What is a major risk of using the `'w'` (Write) mode on a file that already contains data?
options: It will add the new data to the end of the existing content.
It will delete (overwrite) all existing content in the file.
It will open the file in read-only mode instead.
questions.explanation: The `'w'` mode is destructive for existing files; it wipes the file clean as soon as it is opened. If you want to keep existing data, you should use `'a'` (Append) mode instead.

questions.question: Why is it considered a best practice to call the `.close()` method?
options: It is the only way to print the file's content.
It deletes the file from the hard drive to save space.
It tells Python which mode to use for the next file.
It frees up system resources and ensures all data is successfully written to the disk.
questions.explanation: Closing the file is like hanging up a phone call; it tells the Operating System that your program is finished with the resource, preventing memory leaks and data corruption.
